name: Constructivism
visualIdentity: Supplemental design reference, not claimed as a named style in the source collection. Uses forceful diagonals, wedges, circles, blocks, photographic cutouts, and bold typography. Maintain a clear headline and focal point.
suitableUses: Explicit fits include motion posters, calls to action, UI and product storytelling, editorial layouts, and staged geometric compositions. It can suit campaign or launch narratives; suitability beyond listed examples is inferred.
limitations: Avoid recomposition that obscures meaning, unsafe text placement, competing headlines, or transitions that hide causal links. Halftone combinations avoid full-color photos, moiré, and dots over text. Omit pinning if it disrupts layout; keep video independent of scroll. No motion reference is mandatory.
palette: Suggested three-color base for new artwork only: cream background #F4ECD8, black foreground #171717, construction-red accent #C72C2C. Red, black, and cream are suggested, not canonical. Preserve supplied, brand, approved, semantic, and asset colors and role assignments. Use discrete tokens; gradients are disabled. Check actual composited text contrast; do not recolor assets to fix it.
motionAndInteraction: Use directional entrances, cuts, and recomposition along a consistent diagonal while preserving readable holds. Smooth movement may support actions, but keep deliberate cuts and impacts sharp; no automatic bounce. For interactive HTML, scroll may scrub a pinned hero or chapter/story states; release pins without jumps and support backward progress and reduced motion. Video uses deterministic composition time and seekable states, never live input.
audio: No fixed soundtrack or required layer. Choose music, voice, effects, ambience, or silence for the topic and pacing; honor supplied audio choices and assets. Synchronize and mix with picture, preserve speech intelligibility, avoid clipping, and inspect the delivered audio.
assetRequirements: Implementation can combine transparent photographic cutouts, diagonal SVG masks, and real text. Prepare fonts and assets locally. Optional halftone treatment uses black dots on cream, with fixed dot angle and spacing per cutout. Missing asset and source-production details are unspecified.
combinations: Works alone for headlines and calls to action. With style-050 halftones, photographs fit the restricted ink system; keep dots anchored during diagonal movement. With style-093 kinetic typography, heavy condensed sans headlines follow one diagonal family, with red highlighting one word. These are suggestions, not requirements.
productionApproach: HTML/CSS and SVG construct visuals; GSAP is the primary motion engine. HyperFrames owns composition, timing, media/audio sync, validation, and export. Use Remotion only if HyperFrames is unavailable or a verified limitation blocks a required capability, and record why; React alone is not grounds. Optional Motion needs explicit seek synchronization. Keep one owner per animated property; drive video from shared time, preload assets, seed randomness, and verify representative frames and playback. Production-policy responsibilities are explicit; further labor allocation is unspecified.
